questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of Covid, I was obligated to find an exchange destination in Europe. I was sure I would like to go to a bigger city. I never went to Amsterdam before, but the city has such a good reputation and I really liked that the exchange program is 5 fixed courses. The minor I choose also consisted of a lot of laboratory work, which was important to me both because of the upcoming bachelor project, but also because the chances for online teaching was still big and with laboratory courses I was sure I would still get the opportunity to go to uni, as these courses can't be held online.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall I had an amazing exchange! But arriving at a different country is a lot of work. I did not expect it to be so time consuming studying in a different country, mostly because the things excepted of you is different than what I was used to.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Vrije Universitet sends out emails with timelines showing when to do what. I remember thinking it was a bit late to find housing and get information, but I think it is just how it is when going abroad. In general they also responded very quickly to e-mails and was always very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first week was introduction, which was very useful. There was a scavenger hunt on campus and different other activities to navigate on campus, in the city, in your neighborhood and lots of other stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
The introduction week was the best! I met most of my friends in this week and everyone is so open in the beginning of the semester, making it a lot easier to connect compared to a couple of months into the exchange. The introduction program is for all exchange students and master students which makes it possible to meet so many people! 

In the Netherlands they also have a huge student organization called ESN, that makes a ton of different activities in the introduction week and during the entire year.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is difficult and expensive to find housing without help from VU. You have to pay a fee around 2.000 DKK as I remember in order to get housing through the university. Even with help from VU housing I didn't get a room at Uilenstede (Very big campus for students) as it is very popular.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Cornelis Lelylaan - another student accommodation round 4km from city center and 4km from VU. I had my own kitchen and bathroom. In the beginning I was very sad I didn't get a room at Uilenstede, as many parties are held here, but Lelylaan really grew on me and I ended up being so happy about it. I would say that no matter where you live you will find friends and everything is just a small bike ride away, so you can go to parties at Uilenstede and go back when you want to go to bed and don't have to deal with cleaning the next day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you get a room with own bathroom and kitchen you can apply for housing benefit, which actually is a lot of money in the Netherlands. It is not that easy as everything you have to fill out is in dutch, but defiently worth it!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for a minor or you choose your courses yourself. They don't recommend choosing you own, but I would say you can do it anyways. After you register you still have to register for each course in the beginning of each period. The incoming team will help you with it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Incoming team helps with everything regarding exchange, and they replied very quick.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: After the first registration it said that my courses was not available and I couldn't register. This apparently just because I choose I minor. I just had to write to the incoming team and they would register me manually for each course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The 5. semester on VU is called a minor where you usually take 5 courses that all goes well together. The first two courses I took were very basic and I had already learned a lot of it from home, which I was a bit concerned about. However, this gave me the possibility to enjoy my time and not stress too much in the beginning.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the first two courses was a bit basic. The 3 other courses was more similar to the danish level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
They have a lot more to do during the course. In each course we had to hand in at least one report and do one presentation and also have a written exam. It means you have to keep up and follow the course. I only had one course at a time, so I felt like a had to go to the exam all the time (once a month) 

The exams are not as stressfull as at UCPH. You have plenty of time to answer their questions.
They give very good feedback on reports, which I was very happy with, since you spend a lot of time making the reports, and then you don't make the same mistake through all the courses. 
A lot of the presentations and reports are made in groups, which is also different from what I was used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Experimental Cell Biology I 
Experimental Cell Biology II 
Protein to Cell 
Molecular Cell Biology 
Molecular Microbiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially liked Molecular Microbiology. I have never enjoyed microbiology, but through the minor I really learned to love it and this course is so well structured. The course coordinator is a very good teacher. The course has a theoretical part and a practical part. The practicals is helping the molecular microbiology department of VU with a research project, which is so cool! We were divided in small groups of 10 people and with one professor and two student assistens in the lab the practicals were so well structured and you could get as much help as you needed with you project.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When living with own bathroom and kitchen you have to pay a trash tax to the municipality which was around 100-120€ for half a year - but then remember to apply for housing benefit.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport in the Netherlands was very expensive. 
I was  surprised in the beginning of how much money I spend in general because it is expensive to buy all the stuff I needed for the apartment, such as a broom, kitchen stuff, food and so on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many cool things to do in Amsterdam!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You can sign up for a lot of different stuff and they also have very cheap VU gym with many different sports such as kickboxing, spinning, soccer, basket and so on. 
You could sign up for a buddy group, where you were a couple of exchange students together with one dutch student. There was supposed to be one event each month with the buddy group, but because of covid it was limited. However, we went bowling, to dutch quiz night and for walks in the city.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the gym classes with my friends, and also recommend signing up for the buddy group. But most important is the introduction week, it is where everyone meets.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Buy a museums card, so you can visit all the cool museums in ams. I would also recommend traveling around in the netherlands before uni starts (we had one week between introduction and start of classes). This is when the weather is still nice and a lot of the dutch cities just look better when the sun is shining haha

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The dutch culture is very much like the danish

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was more difficult to socialize with dutch students, as they already have their study groups and are well established. Also many of them don't live in Ams but in smaller towns around the city. I would say, don't be disappointed with only getting exchange friends, as it is a lot easier because everyone is open and ready to make new friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: All letters you receive from the municipality is in dutch, which can be challenging and frustrating. You need a DigiD  (like NemID) to pay stuff like taxes and fines. They do a lot of communication by mail (not email) which takes forever and seems very old school.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone speaks English and it is such an International city with so many different cultures. They really enjoy parks and outdoor life, which I think really brings the city to live even though it is winter. They also bike everywhere, and 7km to Uilenstede is not far:)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make as many friends in the beginning before classes starts. 
ENJOY! It is over before you know
The destination is really not that important, you will have a great time no matter where you are.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you want the dorm felling while on exchange I would try getting a room at Uilenstede. 
However, I really enjoyed being able to close my door and have friends and family over in my own apartment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I got a lot lab experience while on exchange, which I am very happy with. the exchange also changed my perspective on microbiology. 
I got a lot of new friends from many different places in Europe. 
I am a lot more confident with speaking English

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from boyfriend, friends and familiy. But ams is not that far away and 5 months is not that long.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: In the beginning I thought 5 months was a really long time, as the semester at VU starts early and ends late. But I was really happy with the length as it made ams fell like my real home and I got used to my everyday life there.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
